advice: Experiment: fuse A transposition with consumption, so each row-major A tile is loaded into ZA once and its transposed vectors feed the four FP32 MOPA accumulators directly. Keep the existing 2VL×2VL output tile and increasing-k accumulation order; do not write a full transposed matrix or packed copy. This removes the separate full-matrix transpose and its scratch allocation from the timed path. For tails, use predicates and in-bounds inactive-vector addresses as in the general path. Hypothesis: avoiding the full transpose write and reread reduces total memory traffic and call cost across n. This is a distinct A-layout experiment; it changes the transpose/consumption boundary rather than packing or MOPA scheduling.
risks: ZA transpose instructions may add enough work or constrain scheduling to outweigh the removed memory traffic. Loading A tiles again for each output-column tile may increase A traffic substantially, especially for large n. Small n may not amortize setup. Validate all supported n, including odd tails and n<=0, against the fixed 0.002 error limit. Measure complete gemm time, including allocation if any, transpose work, and consumption, with fresh serial AC controls and repeated trials; compare the spread without inferring a gain from noisy scores. Keep FP32 arithmetic, ABI, thread count, selector range, and benchmark fixed.
